title: Orders in Two Hands

cast.name: Mateo Salvaterra
cast.portrait: Early twenties in 1991; light-brown skin, short straight black hair neatly combed, dark-brown eyes, a clean-shaven oval face and a serious mouth; plain olive-drab flight suit without patches.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Mateo arrives believing that a country is something a person can belong to completely, and he wants to be worth belonging to. He copies good sentences from speeches into a pocket notebook. He fears being thought disloyal more than he fears being wrong, and has not yet noticed how often those two fears ask him for the same signature.

cast.name: Noemi Arcos
cast.portrait: Early twenties in 1991; warm olive skin, thick dark-brown hair tied back low, black eyes under heavy brows, a narrow face with a crooked half-smile; plain faded khaki flight suit.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Noemi flies better than she speaks to officers, and she speaks to officers very drily. Her mother grows oranges in the hill country, where people have their own opinions about Alendal. Noemi wants to fly without being asked to cheer, and fears the day a form asks her to choose between her family and her wing.

cast.name: Gabriel Tenorio
cast.portrait: Mid thirties in 1991; deep tan skin, close-cropped black hair greying at the temples, brown eyes with heavy creases, a broad nose and thick neck; plain grease-marked grey coveralls.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Gabriel keeps aircraft flying for whoever pays, and on the plateau that is rarely the people who are supposed to. He keeps every receipt on a steel spike above his bench and ties a paper tag to every part saying where it came from. His one unbent rule is that an aircraft's own logbook tells the truth. He fears being asked to apply that rule to people.

cast.name: Sofia Landa
cast.portrait: Late twenties in 1991; medium-brown skin, black hair in a short practical bob, dark-brown eyes, small plain stud earrings and a calm, watchful face; plain pale-blue blouse with an unmarked headset at the neck.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Sofia types the base's reports and keeps a carbon of every page. She has learned that a commander's draft arrives with its conclusion already written, and that the carbon is where she can pencil what actually happened. She wants the other three to trust her pages, and fears that writing what is wanted has already become her handwriting.

1.title: The hangar mouth on the plateau
1.subject: A wide, open hangar mouth on a dry high plateau in early morning light, long shadows across a cracked concrete apron. A tall pole beside the door carries a weathered loudspeaker horn. A small fuel bowser with a few metal drums waits at one side. Inside, a mechanic in grey coveralls kneels beside a wheel removed from a parked, generic aircraft half under a dust sheet; two young people in plain flight suits stand nearby, one holding half an orange. A clipboard of blank sheets rests on an oil drum. Dust in the air; makeshift repair and an unsettled arrival, no markings.

2.title: The operations office
2.subject: A small, plain operations office in mixed lamp and window light: a heavy manual typewriter with a sheet and carbon half rolled in, an old radio set with a desk microphone, and a wall shelf built from mismatched pale wooden crate slats holding stacked folders. A woman is seen from behind at the typewriter; a man in an olive flight suit stands behind her chair, face turned toward the window and the empty apron beyond. No readable writing, maps or screens.

3.title: The stores cage
3.subject: A wire-mesh stores cage inside a hangar, lit by a single hanging lamp over a scarred workbench. Shelves of worn aircraft parts each carry small blank paper tags, some white and some red; a stack of folded grey blankets sits on a lower shelf. A steel spike thick with old receipts stands on the bench beside a disassembled valve. A mechanic in grey coveralls and a woman holding a blank form stand on opposite sides of the bench, faces in partial shadow.

4.title: The gate and the wire
4.subject: A modest air-base gate on a dusty road in late-afternoon light: a plain striped barrier pole, a small guard hut with a bench and a folding table, and a long chain-link fence. A wooden crate of oranges sits on the bench with its lid lifted. A few civilians wait beyond the wire; on the near side a woman in a flight suit stands with her arms folded and her back half-turned, while a man holds an open register. No flags, signs or readable writing.

5.title: The barracks roof at dusk
5.subject: A flat concrete barracks roof at dusk above a quiet airfield, its lights coming on one by one across a dark plateau. Four people sit on upturned wooden crates around a few cardboard boxes of folders tied with string and a paper bag of oranges; the top of a ladder shows at the roof edge. Seen from behind and in profile against a violet sky, with a bare pole silhouetted nearby. No aircraft in the air.

6.title: Both copies on the table
6.subject: A plain operations office in warm late light. Four people of different ages sit close together around a desk on which two neat piles of paper lie side by side, one white and one pale blue, with an old typewriter pushed aside and a paper bag of oranges at one corner. One of them leans in to point at a page while the others listen; nobody salutes or celebrates. Faces partly turned; quiet, earned trust.

7.title: The shelf behind the door
7.subject: A modest office seen through a half-open door. Inside, four figures stand close together with their backs to the doorway, one hand resting on a slatted wooden shelf of folders. In the cool corridor foreground a stranger in a plain coat walks away carrying a single tidy cardboard box. Restrained light and careful distance: protective quiet, not espionage, arrest or a verdict. No readable labels.

8.title: The shelf taken apart
8.subject: An emptied operations office at the end of a day: a bare wall with pale marks where a slatted shelf once hung, loose wooden slats stacked against it, a typewriter under a cloth cover and four separate small bundles tied with string on the desk. Through the window, figures walk away along a dusty road in different directions in long evening light. No body or funeral; a little warm light still in the doorway.

loading_subject: A calm establishing view of a small military airfield on a high, dry plateau at first light: one concrete runway, a few low hangars and barracks, a loudspeaker pole, a chain-link fence and a dusty road winding down toward distant hills planted with orange orchards. Generic aircraft stand under covers without markings, no people in the foreground, and a thin haze lies over the hills.
